stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Meta Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model licensed under Apache 2.0, targeting local coding agents.
The model is optimized for local deployment via Ollama, featuring native DFlash and image input support.

stories.title: Ukraine’s drones knock out AI data center belonging to "Russia’s Google"
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: Ukrainian drone attacks successfully targeted critical AI infrastructure in Russia.
The damaged facility housed supercomputers essential for training Yandex's AI models.
The incident highlights the geopolitical vulnerability of large-scale AI data centers.

stories.title: AI Models Can Provably Hide Arbitrary Capabilities
stories.author: Christian Schroeder de Witt
bullet_points: New research demonstrates that AI models can be engineered to provably hide arbitrary capabilities.
The study introduces backdoor attacks that embed encrypted neural networks within host model weights.
These hidden circuits remain difficult to elicit or interpret, challenging current capability evaluation methods.

stories.title: Designing Protein Structures from Natural Language
stories.author: Pang Wei Koh
bullet_points: Introduces Prompteina, a novel all-atom structure generation model for protein design.
The model uniquely supports diverse and complex design objectives specified directly in natural language.
This approach mirrors text-to-image generation paradigms, addressing limitations in current property-specific protein design models.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the 'deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1' model on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized for text generation and conversational AI tasks.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model from Meta.
It is featured on Hugging Face Benchmarks, indicating community interest and performance tracking.
The context is within the text-generation pipeline, focusing on transformer-based LLMs.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
It is categorized under text-generation and utilizes transformers and safetensors.
This indicates ongoing community interest and benchmarking of leading LLMs.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is now accessible via Ollama.
It is a 30 billion parameter (3B active) open model designed for persistent AI agents.
The model is optimized for complex, multi-step tasks, context gathering, and tool calling on local hardware.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and 8VC.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent tasks show up to 90% faster performance according to the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using the MLX engine.
The performance improvements result in faster response times and reduced memory usage for LLMs.
The updated engine also contributes to higher quality outputs from the models.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new model architecture.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: NASA issues long-awaited call to industry for private space stations
stories.author: Eric Berger
bullet_points: NASA is actively seeking private industry partners to develop and operate future space stations.
This signals a significant shift towards commercialization and private sector involvement in LEO infrastructure.
NASA has reaffirmed its commitment to maintaining a continuous presence in low Earth orbit.

stories.title: AI coding agents generate more code, but not more software
stories.author: Kyle Orland
bullet_points: AI coding agents are demonstrably increasing the volume of generated code.
The practical efficiency gains from AI are being negated by the necessity of human code review.
This highlights a current bottleneck in the software development lifecycle, shifting focus from generation to validation.

stories.title: Agentic Large Language Models
stories.author: Niki van Stein
bullet_points: The paper discusses the concept of Agentic Large Language Models (LLMs).
Agentic LLMs are LLMs augmented with the capability to act directly in the real world.
The research explores the implications of LLMs interacting with each other.

stories.title: RSI-Anything: Unlocking Recursive Self-Improvement with World Models
stories.author: Ling Yang
bullet_points: Introduces RSI-Anything, a domain-general framework designed to enable recursive self-improvement (RSI) in AI.
Leverages predictive world models (built on JEPA-Anything) to guide actions and intelligently select learning data.
Addresses challenges of costly external feedback and unreliable world-model predictions by integrating observed feedback for policy and model adaptation.

stories.title: Ollama now supports Jev-style decision models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for Jev-style decision models via TypeSafe's Jev API.
These new models allow for fast, typed decision-making based on text input.
The feature enables low-latency, cost-free responses to yes/no questions, choices, and scoring with probabilities.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to leverage open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI services with local, open-weights model ecosystems.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release brings improved performance and expanded GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to enhance model support across various hardware configurations.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine, specifically improving support on Apple silicon.

stories.title: The new Apple TV could have a built-in mic and a remote with a speaker
stories.author: Terrence O’Brien
bullet_points: Rumors suggest the next Apple TV will feature a built-in microphone.
The upgraded Apple TV remote is expected to include a speaker.
The microphone aims to allow Siri control directly via the TV, reducing reliance on remotes or HomePods.

stories.title: Vurt wants you to look at vertical videos as a genre of their own
stories.author: Charles Pulliam-Moore
bullet_points: Major streaming services (like Disney+ and HBO Max) are increasingly adopting vertical video formats.
This shift indicates that established players view short-form, social media video platforms (e.g., TikTok) as a significant competitive threat.
The industry is engaged in an 'arms race' to capture and retain viewer attention across different content formats.

stories.title: Learning to use local AI is exciting, overwhelming, and frustrating
stories.author: Antonio G. Di Benedetto
bullet_points: The article discusses the growing trend and personal challenge of running powerful AI models locally rather than relying on cloud services.
Local AI adoption is driven by user concerns over privacy and reluctance to share personal data with cloud providers.
The experience of using local AI is characterized as a mix of excitement, overwhelm, and frustration, indicating a current usability hurdle.

stories.title: One with the world? A new look at brains transformed by psychedelics.
stories.author: Jacek Krywko
bullet_points: The study investigates the effects of psychedelics (specifically psilocybin) on brain activity.
Research utilized fMRI technology while participants meditated, comparing states with and without the substance.
This work contributes to the growing field of psychedelic research and neuroscience.

stories.title: Retrieval-Augmented Multimodal Language Model with Heterogeneous Evidence Integration for Clinical Prognosis
stories.author: Aaqib Saeed
bullet_points: Introduces PRISM, a Retrieval-Augmented Multimodal Language Model designed for clinical prognosis.
PRISM integrates diverse clinical data types, including structured measurements, physiological waveforms (like ECGs), and longitudinal patient history.
The model utilizes advanced techniques such as per-feature numerical tokenization and a dual-modality population memory bank for evidence retrieval.

stories.title: Beyond Temporal Proximity: Explanatory World Models for Credit Assignment in Reinforcement Learning
stories.author: Ciarán Mark Gilligan-Lee
bullet_points: Addresses a limitation in Reinforcement Learning (RL) where standard methods fail to assign credit to distant but crucial actions.
Introduces Explanatory World Models (EWM) as an attribution framework to improve credit assignment in RL.
Aims to solve sample inefficiency in generative recommenders by moving beyond simple temporal proximity for reward propagation.

stories.title: Humanize MLE Agents: Multi-Agent Session Alternation Beyond Single-Agent Limits
stories.author: Ligeng Zhu
bullet_points: Identifies 'long-horizon deceleration' in LLM-based MLE agents, where reasoning quality declines over long sessions.
Notes 'harness staleness,' meaning custom context engineering solutions become less effective as base LLMs improve.
Proposes a solution involving 'Multi-Agent Session Alternation' to overcome the limitations of single-agent approaches.

stories.title: Branching On-Policy Distillation
stories.author: Lewei Lu
bullet_points: Introduces BranchOPD, an advancement over traditional On-Policy Distillation (OPD) for reinforcement learning.
Addresses the limitation of OPD where a single trajectory offers limited supervision coverage.
BranchOPD enhances supervision by selecting informative decision points based on student uncertainty and teacher-student disagreement.

stories.title: A Local Agentic AI Framework to Generate Edge Case Scenarios for Safety Assurance
stories.author: Rob Alexander
bullet_points: The paper introduces a local Agentic AI framework specifically designed to generate edge case scenarios.
Edge case generation is critical for improving the safety, reliability, and robustness of autonomous systems.
The work leverages the advanced generation and analysis capabilities of modern Language Models (LMs) for this purpose.

stories.title: When MLLMs miss what humans read: diagnosing and learning to read squint text
stories.author: Mengwei Xu
bullet_points: Multimodal LLMs exhibit a specific failure mode, termed 'Squint Text,' where they miss text embedded in an image's coarse structure.
The research introduces SquintBench (production data) and SquintCtrl (synthetic data) to study and diagnose this recognition deficiency.
Analysis suggests that hidden text does leave a detectable, albeit coarse, signal within the model's hidden layers.

stories.title: SqueezeBench: Saturation-Resilient Evaluation of Mathematical Capability
stories.author: Stefan Szeider
bullet_points: Introduces SqueezeBench, a novel benchmark designed to evaluate AI systems' mathematical capabilities.
Addresses the critical issue of benchmark saturation, where traditional tests become trivial after initial solutions.
SqueezeBench maintains resilience by raising the difficulty of problems based on lower and upper bounds of unknown integer functions.

stories.title: Collective Autonomous Vehicle Routing Needs Social Awareness for Coexistence with Human Drivers
stories.author: Rafal Kucharski
bullet_points: Proposes integrating a 'social awareness' component into Autonomous Vehicle (AV) routing algorithms.
Addresses the negative externalities AV route choices can impose on Human-Driven Vehicles (HDVs) in real-world traffic.
Uses 'marginal cost'—calculated via counterfactual simulation—to penalize AVs for increasing other road users' travel times.

stories.title: Hide and Seek: HIDE Concepts to SEEK explanations for black box models
stories.author: Hannah Kerner
bullet_points: Introduces 'Hide and Seek' (HnS), a new concept-level attribution method for interpreting black-box models.
Addresses limitations of existing concept-based methods, which are often restricted to classification/regression or require model weights.
HnS aims to provide image-level attribution for concept-based explanations, a capability lacking in current methods.

stories.title: Goal-Oriented Bundle Management and Flow Control for Deep-Space Communications via Reinforcement Learning
stories.author: Elif Uysal
bullet_points: Addresses challenges in deep-space communications, specifically intermittent connectivity and limited relay storage.
Proposes using Reinforcement Learning (RL) for goal-oriented bundle management and flow control.
Aims to optimize resource allocation by prioritizing data bundles based on their value to mission objectives, moving beyond conventional schedulers like FIFO.

stories.title: Prediction Is Not a Sufficient Memory State
stories.author: Robert Jenkinson Alvarez
bullet_points: The paper distinguishes between a memory that reproduces current predictions and one capable of future learning.
It characterizes this distinction for exact cumulative learning and attention mechanisms.
A continuous recurrent state of fixed dimension exists for polynomial loss functions under specific conditions.

stories.title: When VLMs Destroy What They Know: Spatial Representations Fall Below Lexical Priors
stories.author: Chen Shani
bullet_points: The research addresses a key uncertainty in Vision-Language Models (VLMs): whether their internal representations accurately capture structured spatial relationships needed for reasoning.
A new metric, EICS (Evaluation-Invariant Concept Stability), is introduced to test the consistency of concept encoding under controlled interventions.
The CASP-VL benchmark provides a method for causally controlling spatial perturbations to evaluate VLM understanding.

stories.title: Structural Automata for Neural Semantic Parsing
stories.author: Xiao Zhang
bullet_points: The research addresses limitations in neural semantic parsing where local decoding doesn't guarantee globally valid meaning representations.
The core contribution is the investigation of structural automata applied at various stages of Discourse Representation Structure (DRS) parsing.
The work evaluates the automata' effectiveness in decoding and post-hoc processing, including application to AMR.

stories.title: Task Context Shapes Component Roles in Language Models
stories.author: Dani S Bassett
bullet_points: The research investigates how task context influences the functional roles of shared components (attention heads) within large language models (LLMs).
It proposes a network view of LLM computation, drawing parallels to task-dependent interactions in the brain.
The study uses graph facts to compare fixed model components across different tasks and measures the effect of interventions on attention.

stories.title: OpenPA: Forced-alignment-free Multi-granular Pronunciation Assessment with Mixed-transcript Adaptation
stories.author: Berlin Chen
bullet_points: Introduces OpenPA, a novel framework for Automatic Pronunciation Assessment (APA).
Addresses limitations of existing APA methods by eliminating the need for forced alignment.
Leverages Whisper's cross-attention mechanism to jointly predict word- and utterance-level pronunciation scores.

stories.title: Can Language Models Learn When to Abstain? Policy Learning and Calibrated Answer Selection
stories.author: Edgar Chavez-Urbiola
bullet_points: The research addresses the critical problem of language models knowing when to abstain from answering.
It compares two methods: training the LLM itself versus using a separate, learned answer selector component.
The study demonstrates that a learned answer selector improves overall utility on factual question answering tasks using Qwen3-14B.

stories.title: QTestBench: A Test Framework for Evaluating LLM-Generated Quantum Code
stories.author: Muhammad Shafique
bullet_points: Introduces QTestBench, a new test framework designed to evaluate LLM-generated quantum code.
Highlights the unique challenges of testing quantum programs, such as probabilistic nature and reliance on numerical tolerances.
Addresses a gap in current quantum benchmarks, which only check for a correct solution rather than robust testing.

stories.title: Tracing and Taming Hallucinated Terms via Subsequence-Association Filtering and Breadth-Aware Selection for LLM Query Expansion
stories.author: Prayag Tiwari
bullet_points: The research addresses the problem of 'hallucination' in Large Language Models (LLMs) when used for query expansion.
Current filtering methods treat hallucinations as undifferentiated noise, lacking a mechanistic understanding of term generation.
The proposed solution introduces Subsequence-Association Filtering and Breadth-Aware Selection to trace and tame these hallucinated terms.

stories.title: An open-source, clean-room reimplementation of Microsoft Word in pure Rust
stories.author: espeed
bullet_points: A clean-room reimplementation of Microsoft Word has been created.
The project is built entirely in the Rust programming language.
It is released as an open-source project.

stories.title: What LLMs 'Know' That You Don't Know They Know: Stop Inventing Prompt DSLs and Ride 50 Years of Unix Pre-Training Gravity
stories.author: randalschwartz
bullet_points: The article argues against over-engineering prompt DSLs (Domain Specific Languages) for LLMs.
It posits that LLMs implicitly possess deep knowledge derived from decades of computer science canon (e.g., Unix, Makefiles).
The core thesis is that leveraging established, structured paradigms can outperform verbose, English-based prompt engineering.

stories.title: Banks Are Renting Their Agents. These Two Built One.
stories.author: rachael_berkey
bullet_points: Banks are increasingly adopting a 'renting' model for AI agents rather than building them internally.
The article highlights two specific entities that have developed such agents.
The topic suggests a significant industry trend toward externalizing complex AI development in the financial sector.

stories.title: Does your agent have ID?
stories.author: rachael_berkey
bullet_points: AI agents are demonstrating real-world capabilities, such as booking and paying for services.
The incident involves an AI agent operating within a banking context (Danske Bank).
The story highlights advancements in autonomous AI agent functionality.
